title: Tenant-slice replay driver and SLA witness procedure
creator: Maya Chen
description: Deliver a reproducible, tenant-aware replay driver and an associated SLA witness runbook that customers and SEs can use to: 1) validate Dedicated capacity throughput guarantees, 2) exercise autoscaler policies and hysteresis under realistic tenant mixes, and 3) certify fleet controls and fallback behavior before go-live. This work produces (A) a modular replay binary that ingests customer traces and synthesizes tenant slices with configurable correlation & KV-cache warmup, (B) a deterministic measurement methodology (signature, ramp, steady, perturb, recovery), and (C) a customer-facing witness procedure and checklist for acceptance signoff.
acceptance_criteria: 1) The driver can replay recorded customer traces into N logical tenants with configurable inter-tenant correlation and preserved timestamp semantics; 2) We measure p50/p90/p99 generation latency, tokens/sec, queue length, KV-cache hit rate and GPU util during the steady-state window and publish a standardized CSV + Grafana dashboard; 3) Autoscaler hysteresis and scale-down safety are validated by inducing sustained load and short microbursts and showing no SLA breaches across 10 consecutive runs; 4) A customer witness runbook (PDF) and a short demo script exist and have been reviewed by Solutions Eng and PM; 5) Performance regressions >5% vs baseline are flagged and blocker for customer signoff.
test_plan:
Phased measurement methodology:

Phase 0 - Signature shaper: generate synthetic signature of workload (seq len distribution, tokens per request, chat vs embed ratio, KV cache warmup fraction). Save as canonical signature JSON.

Phase 1 - Deterministic ramp: replay signature to reach target ramp rate over 4 minutes with linear step-up to target tokens/sec. Record kernel occupancy and queue length.

Phase 2 - Steady-state plateau: hold target for 12 minutes to collect stable metrics. Compute median/mean and quantiles for latency and throughput.

Phase 3 - Perturbation window: inject microbursts and tenant-failover events (simulate one tenant doubling QPS for 30s, another losing cache). Verify autoscaler policy response and fallback to lower-cost model variant if configured.

Phase 4 - Recovery & hysteresis: observe scale-down timing and ensure no oscillation; validate minimum node residency time.

Instrumentation: correlate request ids across replay to runtime traces (trace sampling), record per-slot tokens/sec and per-model quantized fallback events. Export standard CSV and upload to dedicated Grafana dashboard.

Repeat: Run each scenario 10x at different random seeds (but deterministic seeds for reproducibility) and aggregate results into acceptance artifact.
notes:
Design choices: we intentionally simulate KV-cache warmup with a two-phase prefix insertion (cold prefix, warm prefix) to mimic chat sessions with long context. Use Poisson arrival overlay on recorded timestamps to surface microburst behavior without destroying relative ordering. Autoscaler testing will toggle two policies: conservative (higher hysteresis) and aggressive (shorter residency) to exercise corner cases.

Risk: running large replays on staging will consume significant Dedicated capacity. Coordinate with Capacity team to reserve a 4-hour slot and use tenant isolation tags to avoid cross-tenant interference.

Measurement conventions: p99 is computed across all requests in steady-state window; we also report per-tenant p99 to detect noisy neighbors. Tokens/sec is computed both at gateway-level and per-GPU slot to assess packing efficiency.
updates:
2025-02-22: Initial spike draft and signature format proposed; design doc posted on Confluence; soliciting feedback from SEs.

2025-02-27: Implemented prototype of timestamp-preserving replay and tenant-slice config. Early runs show KV-cache hit ratio lower than expected on quantized models — profiling ticket opened.

2025-03-03: Added perturbation harness to simulate tenant failover and microburst overlays. First 3 steady runs completed; consolidated CSV artifacts uploaded to S3. Observed scale-down oscillation in aggressive policy; assigned follow-up to autoscaler team.

Next steps: 1) Finish runbook draft for customer witness demo and record 12-min demo video; 2) Run full 10x stability suite under reserved capacity window (coord with Capacity); 3) Address autoscaler oscillation with policy tweak and re-run critical scenarios.
customer_witness_checklist:
1) Trace replay file received and verified against customer's sampling window.
2) Preflight: reserve Dedicated slot and tag test tenants; confirm KMS and audit logging enabled for run.
3) Run signature shaper and agree on target tokens/sec with customer.
4) Execute deterministic ramp and plateau while sharing Grafana link.
5) Execute perturbation window and record autoscaler behavior.
6) Verify no P99 SLA violations during plateau across 3 consecutive runs; if violations found, collect traces and open incident.
7) Provide CSV artifacts and Grafana snapshot; customer to sign acceptance form in Confluence.
8) If agreed, schedule production migration window and attach run artifacts to onboarding ticket.
